summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis and liver transplant was admitted with fever and right upper quadrant abdominal pain. Given her immunosuppressed state, she was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics. Imaging, including CT and MRCP, showed no evidence of infection, biliary obstruction, or appendicitis, though a stable soft tissue density near the abdomen was noted. Blood cultures and viral studies were negative, and autoimmune workup was unremarkable. Antibiotics were discontinued after 48 hours without recurrence of fever. She developed right lower quadrant pain during admission, which improved without surgical intervention. Her symptoms were attributed to post-transplant changes, possibly related to embolization coils or scar tissue. She was discharged home on tramadol and ondansetron for symptomatic management, with no changes to her baseline immunosuppressive regimen.
